plan: Trim SPY to 20% to cure concentration and reduce broad index risk.
Sell QQQI, QQQ, CRWD, and SMH to exit downtrending positions.
Sell SOXL and SPAL to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy MSFT at 10% as a top-quality long setup for capital preservation.
Maintain a significant cash buffer for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a realistic outlook of ~1.5% per month. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by cutting all leveraged ETFs and downtrending positions, reducing concentration, and favoring high-quality setups. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure concentration and reduce broad index risk.
Sell QQQI, QQQ, and SMH to exit downtrending positions.
Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy SNOW at 4% as a quality tech long setup.
Maintain a cash buffer of ~10% for flexibility.
balanced.read: This balanced plan prioritizes risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech. The plan aims for a moderate risk profile with controlled drawdowns, balancing growth potential with capital protection.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure concentration while maintaining exposure.
Sell QQQI, QQQ, and SMH to exit downtrending positions.
Add SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy SNOW at 6% as a high-scoring tech long setup.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer (~5%) and use strict stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% per month by leaning into leverage and high-scoring setups. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk, especially with leveraged ETFs subject to decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the amplified losses possible with this approach.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index exposure and free up capital.
Add QQQI to 30% to significantly increase income-generating exposure.
Sell QQQ, CRWD, SMH, SOXL, and SPAL to eliminate growth-oriented and leveraged positions.
Focus on steady monthly distributions with a low drawdown priority.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability and future income opportunities.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by prioritizing steady monthly distributions. It rotates heavily into income ETFs and broad index, cutting leverage and high-beta names to near zero. While aiming for low drawdown, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market selloffs; this is not a savings account.
